headline: EXPORT SALES AT 7:30; BEANS HOLD, CRUDE RUNS
subheadline: Pro Farmer's final tour day sets up this morning's export print as the week's last live catalyst.
lead: Beans added a dime and a half to $12.25, corn sat dead flat at $4.77, and crude ran nearly 3% to $86.86 as Iranian supply routes fracture further. The export sales number at 7:30 AM CT is the last data point that can move this week's grain story. Tour results have run below last year; the question is whether buyers care.
the_takeaway: Wait for 7:30. Export sales decide whether beans hold $12.25 or give it back.
teaser: Tour wraps, export sales print at 7:30 CT. Beans are holding; crude is running on Iranian supply fractures.

one_number.context: Middle Eastern oil demand has pushed very large crude carrier prices above $130 million, per the Financial Times. That freight cost eventually lands on diesel at the farm gate; the Hormuz squeeze is now a tanker market story, not just a crude price story.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called beans up toward $12.16; beans closed $12.25 yesterday, through the level.
yesterdays_call.note: Two straight hits on beans. The fund and technical buying narrative held; don't chase it into 7:30.

sections.title: BEANS FIRM, CORN FLAT
sections.body:
- Soybeans added 1.5 cents to **$12.25**, quiet on the surface, but yesterday's 21.5-cent session showed the fund and technical buyers are still present; tour results running below last year gave them the excuse.
- November beans at $12.40 keep carry working old-crop into new-crop, no spread warning yet.
- Corn at $4.77 flat for the session; Dec at $5.02 hasn't moved, and with tour ear counts not yet fully in, the board is simply waiting.
sections.catalyst: Pro Farmer tour results running below year-ago; fund and technical buying lifted soybeans sharply Wednesday.
sections.bottom_line: Beans have momentum and a story; corn is in a holding pattern until tour wraps and exports print.
sections.vs_yesterday: Beans: yesterday's 21-cent session consolidated, not reversed.

sections.title: EXPORT SALES: 7:30 AM CT
sections.body:
- Weekly export sales print at 7:30 AM CT; beans under 300K MT would say the Wednesday rally was position-squaring, not demand-driven.
- China is buying, per the Minnesota Soybean Growers Association and confirmed sales earlier this week, but the China purchase commitment (May 18 deal, through 2028) has shown a buy-the-rumor-sell-the-fact pattern that caps follow-through.
- Corn export pace is the secondary read; a strong number could finally give the flat corn board a reason to move.
sections.catalyst: USDA Weekly Export Sales release, 7:30 AM CT today; China soybean buying active per grower association comments.
sections.bottom_line: Beans above 300K MT confirms demand is real; below that, the chart is doing the work alone.
sections.farmer_action: Old-crop corn: if export sales print above 500K MT on corn, that is your window to re-evaluate holds before harvest pressure builds.

sections.title: CRUDE RUNS ON HORMUZ FRACTURES
sections.body:
- WTI ran 2.8% to **$86.86**, the biggest single-session move in several weeks, driven by reports that Iranian crude exports are now effectively blocked and Chinese refiners are scrambling for Iraqi barrels.
- Supertanker prices hit all-time highs above $130M; the Iran-Hormuz cycle, a pattern of escalation and premium deflation running since early spring, appears to be in a re-escalation leg with less optimism about a quick resolution.
- Natural gas eased to $2.75, not a concern for fall fieldwork; diesel tightness remains the input-cost story to watch.
sections.catalyst: Iranian crude exports effectively halted per Rapidan Energy; supertanker VLCC prices hit record highs; Chinese refiners buying Iraqi crude.
sections.bottom_line: Crude at $86.86 is a diesel problem for fall fieldwork; watch crack spreads, not the headline WTI number.

sections.title: CATTLE EASE, DAIRY STEADY
sections.body:
- Live cattle slipped 0.9% to **$222.97** and feeders dropped 1.0% to $336.40; Wednesday's news said feeders led lower on corn strength, which fits the math.
- The Cargill multi-plant lockout, with roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity still removed, keeps the packer margin story front-and-center; the processing constraint, not cattle numbers, is still the binding factor.
- Class III Milk barely moved at $16.65; a three-day pause on Section 338 tariffs against Canada's dairy TRQs adds a policy wrinkle, but no price signal yet.
sections.catalyst: Corn strength pressured feeder margins Wednesday; USDA suspended Section 338 tariffs on Canada for three days over dairy TRQ dispute.
sections.bottom_line: Cattle are drifting, not breaking; the Aug 24 Mexican port reopening at Douglas, AZ is the next structural catalyst.
sections.vs_yesterday: Cattle: Cargill deal framing from yesterday, lockout still ongoing, no resolution update.

outside_the_pit.title: Tyson Faces WARN Act Investigation After Plant Closures
outside_the_pit.body: A law firm is investigating whether Tyson provided legally required notice before closing its Joslin and Eagle Mountain beef facilities. If violations are found, it adds legal cost to an already processing-constrained beef sector and could slow any capacity restoration timeline.

outside_the_pit.title: More Milk Supply Coming; Demand Story Is the Question
outside_the_pit.body: Dairy Herd reports milk production is trending up heading into fall, raising the question of whether demand growth can absorb the volume. Class III near $16.65 is not pricing a surplus yet, but producers adding cows into a softening price environment should run the numbers.

weekly_thread.question: What will Pro Farmer scouts find, and does the tour push December corn above $4.90 or back below $4.75 by Friday?
weekly_thread.status_text: Tour results have run below year-ago on both crops; December corn sits at $5.02, but export sales at 7:30 AM CT today are the last live catalyst before Friday's final tour number.

the_more_you_know.title: WHY 300K MT IS THE BEAN DEMAND LINE
the_more_you_know.body: USDA counts export sales in metric tons. Soybeans need roughly 300K MT per week to stay on pace for the USDA's current 1.97 billion bushel export forecast. Miss that line today and the math starts to argue with the chart -- which already ran 21.5 cents Wednesday.

watch_list.desc: USDA Weekly Export Sales: soybeans above 300K MT confirms demand is real; below that, Wednesday's rally was position-squaring.
Pro Farmer national crop tour number: December corn above $4.90 requires scouts to find ears below 182 bu/acre equivalent; above that, the range holds.
Douglas, AZ port reopening for Mexican feeder cattle: watch the feeder/live spread as the first phased imports begin pricing returning supply.
WTI above $87 extends the diesel cost concern for fall fieldwork; watch the diesel crack spread, not the crude headline.

daily_quote.text: The only constant in life is change.
